subject: C32
required_fixes: R1 — apps/desktop/src/v2/harness/harness.tsx:294 and :448; crates/desktop-core/src/authority/harness_tools.rs:218; crates/desktop-core/src/harness/session.rs:1617: production approvals are all handled by the same in-page allow action, and every mcpTool is described as read-only. The core approval path checks binding/grants but carries no authoritative read/write classification or native-confirmation branch. A mutating MCP call is therefore presented with the false assurance that nothing changes; the native-sheet guarantee explicitly required by C32 and D058 is not implemented. Classify effects authoritatively, show truthful scope/effect information, and enforce the specified native confirmation for write-capable calls. Acceptance: production-interface and native tests distinguish read-only and mutating calls, prove in-page consent alone cannot authorize the write path, and preserve stale-call/grant rejection.

R2 — apps/desktop/src/v2/harness/harness.tsx:69 and :95: the first-send continuation stores only text, discards the start receipt's operation ID, consumes any ready conversation, and clears the draft before sendHarness is admitted. A refused first send loses the message; a failed startup leaves pending set and Send permanently disabled; a later replacement conversation can consume the old pending message. Bind the continuation to the admitted conversation/context/workspace, preserve editable text until confirmed admission, and retire pending work on failure or replacement without automatic replay. Acceptance: test refused/unknown first sends, failed startup and conversation/workspace replacement, with recoverable text, usable controls and no send to an unrelated operation.

R3 — apps/desktop/src/v2/harness/harness.tsx:138 and :197: New investigation only focuses the existing composer; the next Send still targets the current conversation. The contextual Start a new investigation writes to NEXT while a live conversation keeps the composer bound to its own ID, so the requested prefill can remain invisible. Implement an explicit transition to a separate new investigation while preserving the old transcript and respecting pending decisions. Acceptance: with a live conversation present, both entry points lead to a different conversation ID, and contextual restart visibly preserves the opening question.

R4 — apps/desktop/src/v2/harness/harness.tsx:64 and :258: the re-skin ignores ConversationView.unsent and signInFailure. Gateway/MCP renewal failure and confirmHarnessWrite allow=false return the message in the core, but it never returns to the composer. The button Keep it read-only also misdescribes allow=false: the core gives the job back without changing project access. Restore the returned message and failure explanation, and align the decline action's label/behavior with the retained authority contract. Acceptance: failed renewal and declined write renewal preserve the exact unsent text, explain that nothing was sent, and neither resend automatically nor claim an access change that did not occur.

R5 — apps/desktop/src/v2/harness/harness.tsx:211, :316 and :432: conversation failure, lastTurn, cleanup and non-declined entry states are not presented. Failed/truncated/interrupted answers can look complete, and every failed or ended conversation announces that its transcript is saved even when savedAt is null or saveFailure is set. Restore truthful outcome/status presentation, including the retained failed-turn uncertainty warning, and derive saved claims from actual save evidence. Acceptance: tests for startup failure, failed/truncated/interrupted turns, failed cleanup and failed saving show distinct accessible outcomes and never falsely announce a saved transcript.

R6 — apps/desktop/src/v2/harness/harness.tsx:64; apps/desktop/src/v2/v2-shell.tsx:295: drafts live only in component state, which is destroyed on destination navigation or context-key remount. A draft disappears when the operator visits Administration and returns. This does not meet state-ownership.md's Harness store/per-conversation lifetime or the required tenant round-trip behavior. Keep transient drafts in a tenant/workspace/conversation-scoped presentation store, without reviving retired execution authority. Acceptance: navigation away/back and tenant A/B/A preserve each scope's draft without cross-scope disclosure or automatic sending.

R7 — packages/desktop-contracts/fixtures/wire/harness-lifecycle-mcp.json; docs/architecture/ui-v2/provenance.md:60; apps/desktop/src/v2/harness/harness.test.tsx:95: the required GatewayRead::McpServers lifecycle has been replaced by a hand-authored workspace_inventory.list_mcp_servers remote-tool snapshot, with no implementation or fixture adapter establishing that capability. P47 contradicts C32 milestone 2, screens/harness.md and P16. Its proposed pii-check guardrail also claims to deny non-allowlisted MCP servers without expressing an MCP allow-list rule. Implement and test the admitted read specified by the reviewed contract, or obtain a reviewed requirement change, and make the recommendation describe the actual proposed policy. Acceptance: a production-interface fixture exercises the specified Gateway catalog read and its approve/decline/follow-up paths, with an honestly described valid guardrail; parser acceptance and pushed snapshots alone are insufficient.
